newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock exchange rises in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock exchange rises in quiet trade.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose slightly on Wednesday in quiet trade and brokers said they expected optimism over Israel's deal on Palestinian self-rule should last into next week's trading.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.21 points to 153.21 in turnover worth 573,000 dinars.
Trade is traditionally light in the Moslem holy month of Ramadan with few buyers around, and nearly half of Wednesday's trade was taken up by heavyweight Arab Bank, which rose 0.25 dinars to 259.00.
"The market hasn't responded that much to the good news," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah. "I think the response will be shown early next week."
Other heavily traded shares were Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturers, Arab Pharmaceuticals and Unified Transport Company.
All three companies, which rose slightly, are expected to benefit from increased food and medicine exports to neighbouring Iraq under last month's oil-for-food deal.
Gaining shares outnumbered losers by 16 to 10. Shares in 14 companies traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.04 percent to 82.24 points.
